title: Find a LinkedIn Profile URL from a Name and Company
summary: How go-to-market teams and their coding agents resolve LinkedIn profile URLs from a name and company with Cargo: linkedin.findProfileUrl returns a URL only when exactly one profile matches, then a validation step confirms the current employer. Why the found rate is low, and why that is the point.
body_markdown:
**To find a LinkedIn profile URL from a name and company, run Cargo’s` linkedin.findProfileUrl` action with` fullName` and` companyName` , then enrich each URL it returns and keep it only if the profile’s current company is the one you expected. Expect a URL for roughly one row in four: the action answers only when exactly one LinkedIn profile matches, and a miss costs 0 credits.**


That is the[find-linkedin-url](https://www.getcargo.ai/skills/find-linkedin-url) skill for go-to-market lists: resolve, then validate, and leave a row empty rather than guess.


## What 72k lookups show#


Cargo platform data, 90 days to Oct 16 2026:


Measure Value


Name-to-LinkedIn-URL runs 72,240, across 47 workspaces


Runs that returned a URL 23.9%


Credits charged on misses 0, on every miss


Credits per URL found 0.25


## Why the found rate is low#


The action is strict by design. It runs a LinkedIn people search for the exact phrase of the full name **and** the exact phrase of the company name, and it returns a profile only when that search resolves to a single person. Two results is not a match, it is a miss. So is zero. The common reasons a real person does not come back:


- **The name is not written the way the profile writes it.** A nickname (Bill for William), a dropped middle name, a maiden name, missing accents.
- **The company is not written the way the profile writes it.** A legal name against a brand (“Alphabet” for “Google”), a suffix (“Acme Inc”), an old name after a rebrand.
- **The person has moved on.** CRM records age; the profile now shows a new employer.
- **The name is common.** Two Sam Lees at the same company is an ambiguous search, and the action refuses to pick one.


The trade is deliberate: a missing URL costs a row, while a wrong URL attaches someone else’s profile, history and contact details to your contact. Clean the inputs before running (the name as it appears on LinkedIn, the company’s brand name) rather than loosening the match.


## Run it#


### 1. Install and sign in


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com                   # sends a code
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com   --code   123456     # creates the account on first use


```


No LinkedIn account is needed: the lookup runs on identities Cargo operates and bills credits.


### 2. Resolve a candidate URL


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"linkedin","actionSlug":"findProfileUrl"}'   \
--records   '[{"fullName":"Ada Lovelace","companyName":"Analytical Engines"}]'   \
--limit   5   --wait-until-finished


```


` --limit 5` pilots the first five rows.` companyName` is optional, but without it only the name is searched, and a name alone is rarely unique. A found row returns` linkedin_profile_url` ,` full_name` ,` current_title` ,` headline` ,` company_name` and` location` ; a miss returns nothing and is not charged.


### 3. Validate it


A single search hit can still be the wrong person: the company phrase can match a past employer or a line in the headline (“ex-Analytical Engines”). Enrich each found URL and compare the current employer to your record:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"linkedin","actionSlug":"enrichProfile"}'   \
--records   '[{"linkedinUrl":"https://www.linkedin.com/in/ada-lovelace-example"}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


Read` company` ,` company_domain` and the` experiences` entry with` is_current` set. Keep the URL when` company_domain` matches the domain you hold for the account (or the current experience’s company matches by name); write the row back as unresolved when it does not.` enrichProfile` costs 0.25 credits per profile returned.


### One call instead of two


` linkedin.enrichProfileFromName` runs the same strict search and returns the full enriched profile in one step, for 0.5 credits when it finds someone and 0 when it does not. It takes` name` and` companyName` . Use it when you want the profile anyway; use the two steps when most rows will miss, since misses on the first step are free and the second step only runs on the hits.


## What it costs#


Action Credits Charged when


` linkedin.findProfileUrl` 0.25 a URL is returned


` linkedin.enrichProfile` 0.25 a profile is returned


` linkedin.enrichProfileFromName` 0.5 a profile is returned


At the 23.9% platform found rate, 1,000 rows cost about 60 credits to resolve and about 60 more to validate the hits: roughly 0.5 credits per URL found, and nothing for the rows that miss.


Once you hold the URL,[enrich the LinkedIn profile](https://www.getcargo.ai/skills/enrich-linkedin-profile) for the rest of the record, or find the person’s[work email](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/find-and-verify-work-emails-at-scale) .


## Frequently asked questions#


The action returns a URL only when the exact name and exact company resolve to a single LinkedIn profile. Ambiguous and empty searches both return nothing. Across 72,240 runs in the 90 days to Oct 16 2026, 23.9% returned a URL.

Yes, if a wrong match matters to you. The search can match the company in a past role or the headline. Enrich the profile and check that the current company domain is the one you hold.
